- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days of negative sentiment + falling prices, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent highs/lows to anchor forecast.
